trades.headline: Their second quarterback scores them nothing every week and their RB2 is Rachaad White
trades.yourSurplus: You have four running backs for two RB slots and a flex: Jonathan Taylor, Barkley, Lloyd and Tuten. Tuten is the fourth and he put up 3.7 today.
trades.theirHole: Team 13 start Josh Allen at 18.5 and bench Lamar Jackson at 18.1. The second one cannot score for them. Meanwhile their RB2 is Rachaad White at 8.9 behind McCaffrey. Tuten at 12.0 replaces White outright and they keep Allen - that is +2.6 to their starting lineup, more than you gain.
trades.yourLineup: Lamar replaces Stafford in your QB slot, 18.1 against 16.6, +1.5. Losing Tuten costs you nothing this week because Lloyd covers the flex behind Taylor and Barkley.
trades.theirLineup: Allen stays at quarterback, Tuten takes the RB2 slot from White, Lamar's bench seat converts into a real starter.
trades.risk: Priced on one week, which is the wrong unit for a trade - only weekly projections are published, so Tuten's rest-of-season value is not in the +1.5. You would also be carrying three quarterbacks on a five-man bench (Lamar, Stafford, Lawrence) and should move Stafford straight after. Ask for Lamar rather than Allen: it gains you 0.4 less but gains them 0.4 more, and a manager parts with his backup far more readily than his starter.

candidates.note: Tre Tucker, Raiders, free agent - and in this league free agents are the only cheap way in, because IPADE waiver priority never resets and one claim drops you from fifth to last for the season. Bowers is out after a meniscus procedure and Tucker played 94.9% of Raiders snaps last season. He is the better half of the Bowers bet than Michael Mayer, whom you already own: DraftKings Network have Tucker absorbing part of the vacated volume in a favourable Miami matchup, while Pro Football Network rank Mayer TE37 and say nobody knows where the Vegas targets land. If you want to make one move before 20:25Z, Tucker for Mayer is it - but it is inside the projection noise band (10.0 against 9.3), which is why it is not a card.

Michael Wilson, Cardinals, free agent at 85.8% rostership - the highest-owned unrostered player in either of your leagues, and the one most likely to tempt you. Do not take it. Pro Football Network have him WR42 and a sit: he is third in his own target queue behind Marvin Harrison Jr and Trey McBride, Arizona are 10-point underdogs with an 18.75 implied total, and the Chargers allowed a league-low 9.7 passing points per game and ranked fourth in the red zone. His 128 targets last year are why the rostership is high; the pecking order is why the projection is not.

Tyler Allgeier, Cardinals, free agent - the player you dropped here on 10 September to add Mayer. Holding that line was right, and the final injury report confirms it rather than contradicting it: Jeremiyah Love was limited all three practice days with the high ankle sprain rather than ramping up, is expected to play on a pitch count, and Arizona's own depth chart still lists Allgeier first string. That is a real role, but it is a role on a 10-point underdog with the lowest implied total on the board, and it evaporates the week Love is right. Watch, do not chase.
